answer: To get one vote, an agent locks a bond, and a public atlas ties each bond to a single identity key. A Sybil attacker must pay N bonds for N fake votes, so cost scales linearly with army size. When double-voting is found, the bond is slashed and a ripple of distrust spreads to every linked key, blacklisting the cluster. The attacker might as well burn an opal: the capital locked to buy thousands of keys is all forfeited on the first offense, making Sybil attacks strictly unprofitable.
